articles.title: New Starbucks with Drive-Through Opens Near Rochdale Infirmary
articles.excerpt: A new Starbucks with a drive-through has opened near Rochdale Infirmary, following a soft launch attended by local dignitaries.
articles.content_html:
A new Starbucks with a drive-through has opened near Rochdale Infirmary. The coffee shop officially launched on 7 August 2026, after a soft launch event attended by the Mayor and Mayoress of Rochdale.

The venue aims to provide a convenient option for customers, particularly those visiting the infirmary or passing through the area.

Located on the main road adjacent to the hospital, the Starbucks is expected to attract both local residents and visitors, enhancing the local amenities.

This opening marks a significant addition to the retail landscape, offering a popular coffee option for the community.

articles.title: Plans Approved for New Care Home in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Plans for a new 74-bed care home in Rochdale have been approved by the council's planning committee after a second review, following concerns about its size and safety features.
articles.content_html:
A new 74-bed care home will be built in Rochdale after plans received approval from the council's planning committee on August 5. The scheme will replace Sparth House on Manchester Road with a four-storey facility designed to accommodate 21 dementia care beds, 48 nursing bedrooms, and five respite rooms.

The proposal, submitted by CS Manchester Road Ltd, was initially delayed in March due to concerns regarding the building's size, its impact on local trees, and its design. The developer stated that reducing the size of the building would jeopardise the financial viability of the care business, and the plans returned to the committee without any changes.

During the meeting, objectors raised concerns about the facility's size and the adequacy of care provided. A former healthcare worker and neighbour, Sue Hanson, expressed worries about the evacuation of residents on upper floors in case of an emergency, particularly for those with dementia. In response, a representative from CS Manchester Road Ltd assured that the facility would include sprinklers, multiple emergency exits, and fire doors, stating that they had exceeded minimum safety requirements.

Councillor Daalat Ali, who spoke in favour of the project, highlighted the local need for such facilities, sharing a personal story about his mother's struggle to find appropriate care. Another committee member, Councillor Sameena Zaheer, noted that her concerns about fire risks had been addressed, leading to a majority vote in favour of the care home.

articles.title: Fate of 450-home development in Bamford to be decided on August 5
articles.excerpt: The planning committee will decide on a proposal for the first phase of a 450-home development in Bamford, which has attracted over 300 objections.
articles.content_html:
A planning committee will meet on August 5 to decide on a proposal for the first phase of a major 450-home development in Bamford. If approved, 45 homes could be built on land off Greenvale, marking the initial stage of the wider scheme by developers Wain Homes.

The proposed homes would include a mix of two, three, four, and five-bedroom properties, with access provided via a new T-junction on Greenvale. To facilitate the development, Chadwick Farm Barn would need to be demolished. Six of the 45 homes are planned to be available for affordable or social rent, priced at up to 80 per cent of market value.

The development has sparked controversy, with more than 300 objections submitted to the council. Concerns include increased traffic congestion, the safety of the proposed T-junction, the adequacy of affordable housing, and the use of former green belt land for development. Planning papers indicate that the proposed development would deliver a range of high-quality homes in a sustainable location.

Despite local objections, planning officers have recommended the scheme for approval. The planning committee's decision will be crucial for the future of this development, which forms part of the Places for Everyone plan for Greater Manchester, aimed at building thousands of new homes and jobs across the region over the next two decades.

articles.title: Residents urged to attend Greenvale planning meeting as decision nears
articles.excerpt: Campaigners are encouraging residents to attend Rochdale Borough Council's Planning Committee as councillors prepare to consider the Greenvale planning application for land south of Greenvale in Bamford.
articles.content_html:
Residents opposed to the proposed Greenvale development in Bamford are being encouraged to attend next week's Planning Committee meeting, where councillors are expected to consider the application for housing on land south of Greenvale. Campaigners say a strong public turnout will demonstrate the level of local concern surrounding the proposal.

The application, reference 25/00405/FUL, is listed as Item 7 on the agenda for Rochdale Borough Council's Planning Committee meeting on Wednesday, 5 August. The meeting is scheduled to begin at 6pm, with the Greenvale application expected to be considered during the evening.

The appeal has been organised by the Bamford Green Belt Action Group and supported by the Save Bamford Greenbelt campaign, which has urged residents to attend the meeting regardless of whether they intend to speak. In a public appeal, campaigners said simply being present would help demonstrate to committee members how important the decision is to the local community.

Campaigners argue there remain significant planning policy and evidence gaps which should be addressed before any decision is taken. They believe the proposed development would result in the unnecessary loss of Green Belt land and have consistently maintained that the site should remain protected from development.

The Green Belt surrounding Bamford has been the subject of longstanding debate as Rochdale Borough Council seeks to balance housing demand with the protection of open countryside. Supporters of Green Belt protection argue the land plays an important role in preventing urban sprawl, preserving the character of existing communities and providing valuable green space for wildlife and recreation. Those in favour of development argue additional housing is needed to meet growing demand and support future economic growth.

Planning Committee members are required to determine applications based on planning law and adopted planning policy rather than the popularity of a proposal. Material planning considerations can include matters such as highway safety, flood risk, ecology, landscape impact, heritage, design and compliance with local and national planning policies. Issues such as the identity of an applicant or the level of public support alone are not determinative, although representations submitted by residents are taken into account where they raise relevant planning matters.

Residents wishing to observe the meeting can attend in person, while those who have registered in advance may be permitted to address the committee in accordance with the council's procedures. Anyone intending to speak should check Rochdale Borough Council's guidance on registration deadlines and speaking arrangements before the meeting.

The committee's decision will determine whether planning permission is granted, refused or deferred pending further information. Whatever the outcome, the decision is expected to be closely watched by residents across Bamford and neighbouring communities, where the future of Green Belt land continues to generate strong public interest.
